'''Maurice Janet''' (1888–1983) was a French mathematician.

==Education and career==
In 1912, as a student he visited the [[University of Göttingen]].<ref>Laurent Mazliak (ed.), Le voyage de Maurice Janet à Göttingen. Carnet de voyage (automne 1912), Les Éditions Materiologiques 2013</ref> He was a professor at the [[University of Caen]]. He was an Invited Speaker of the [[International Congress of Mathematicians]] in 1924 in [[Toronto]], in 1932 in [[Zürich]], and in 1936 in [[Oslo]].

Named in his honor are [[Janet basis|Janet bases]], Janet sequences<ref>[https://arxiv.org/abs/1306.2818 ''The mathematical foundations of general relavity revisited'' by Jean-François Pommaret, 2013]</ref><ref>[https://arxiv.org/abs/1210.2675 ''A pedestrian approach to Cosserat/Maxwell/Weyl theory'' by Jean-François Pommaret, 2012]</ref> and a related algorithm in the theory of systems of partial differential equations.<ref>{{cite book|author=Robertz, Daniel|title=Formal Algorithmic Elimination for PDEs|volume=2121|publisher=Springer|year=2014|page=7|doi=10.1007/978-3-319-11445-3|series=Lecture Notes in Mathematics|isbn=978-3-319-11444-6}}</ref> In 1926, he proved results that were later generalized by [[John Forbes Nash Jr.]] in his [[Nash embedding theorem|embedding theorem]].

In 1948, Janet was the president of the [[Société Mathématique de France]].  He was a close friend of the mathematician [[Ernest Vessiot]].
